description: BASELINE: 6-layer ternary GPT (fast-A geometry: hidden=512, heads=8, ff=1408, ~44.7M params, 19.3M trits + 25.2M FP embeddings). Recipe transferred from HRM champion: random scales lognormal frozen, freeze non-embed FP, CMuon-STE cautious lr=0.20 cosine, default 70/25/5 mix, 5000 steps. val 4.0645 — BEATS HRM r042 Phase A (same recipe at fast-A) by -0.073 nats AT HALF THE WALL TIME (7877s vs ~15000s for HRM). Confirms recurrence-free GPT is the right autoresearch substrate for ternary speedups. Trajectory still descending at step 5000 (last 500 -0.027). New ternary-nanoGPT leaderboard floor.

Q-K=V (arxiv 2606.04032): share W_K and W_V projections. Param count 44.74M → 43.14M (-1.60M, -8pct of trits). val 4.1335 vs g001 4.0645 = +0.069 nats (+1.7pct PPL, well below the +5pct pass bar; paper reported +2.48pct at 1.2B). Wall 7691s vs g001 7877s = -2.4pct (one fewer projection per attention block). PROMOTED to baseline: all future runs use --share-kv unless explicitly ablated.

Phase 1 #2: CMuon momentum dtype bf16 (was fp32). val 4.1281 vs g002 4.1335 = -0.005 nats (noise). Wall +180s (~+2.3pct, slight dtype-cast overhead in EMA update). PROMOTED to baseline. Memory: CMuon m buffer for 17.7M trits drops 70.8MB→35.4MB. bf16 dtype keeps fp32 range; only mantissa truncated. NS5 still fp32 internally.

CMuon LR sweep leg 1: muon-lr=0.30 (up from g003's 0.20). val 4.1609 vs g003 4.1281 = +0.033 nats (+0.8pct). lr=0.30 WORSE → optimum at or below 0.20, sweep down to 0.15 next. Note: SIGINT'd at step 4430 to validate resume path; trainer auto-resumed cleanly from interrupted.pt and ran to step 5000. Discovered minor harness issue: tee truncated train.log on resume (lost pre-SIGINT vals); fixed with tee -a in this commit. Wall is approximate combined (7063s pre + 1141s post). Discard from leaderboard.

CMuon LR sweep leg 2: muon-lr=0.15 (down from g003's 0.20). val 4.1147 vs g003 4.1281 = -0.013 nats (best so far). 0.15 IS better than 0.20 → optimum below 0.20, continue down to 0.10. Hybrid run: bs=2 ga=16 for first 3635 steps (1.55s/it), bs=4 ga=8 for the resume tail (much faster wall, same effective batch 32). interrupted.pt-based resume across batch shape change works. tee -a harness fix preserved both segments in train.log. bs=4 ga=8 adopted as new baseline going forward.

CMuon LR sweep leg 3: muon-lr=0.10 with bs=4 ga=8 (full bs=4 from scratch). val 4.1327 vs g005 0.15 = +0.018 nats (worse). LR optimum BRACKETED: 0.30 (4.16) > 0.20 (4.13) > 0.15 (4.11) > 0.10 (4.13) — g005 lr=0.15 is the GPT optimum. Wall 7565s ≈ g005's combined ~7773s and g003's bs=2 7877s — bs=4 saves ~5pct kernel-launch overhead at this scale, not 2x. Total wall is dominated by tokens-per-step which is constant across bs/ga splits of effective batch 32. Discarded from leaderboard.

Phase 1 #7b: effective-batch sweep. lr=0.15 + bs=2 ga=32 (eff batch 64 vs g005's 32). val 4.0085 vs g005 4.1147 = -0.106 nats (-2.5pct) — NEW CHAMPION at fixed-step protocol. Wall 15172s = 2x g005 (linear in tokens per step at fixed step count). Better val per step, but per-WALL the tradeoff may not be favorable; eff=32 at 10000 steps would likely beat eff=64 at 5000 steps for similar wall. Keeping eff=32 as practical baseline (faster iteration), recording eff=64 as best-known reference.

Phase 5a: TRITISE THE EMBEDDINGS. 42.9M of 43.5M params now ternary (98.6pct ternary, FP residual 0.68M = norms + scales). val 4.7801 vs g005 baseline 4.1147 = +0.665 nats (+16pct). Trajectory still descending at step 5000 (-0.027 last 500). KEY: trajectory SLOPES are IDENTICAL (g008 -1.46 nats / 4500 steps vs g005 -1.46 / 4500). The gap is a FLAT OFFSET from worse init — random ternary embedding starts at val 6.24 vs random-normal embedding 5.57. Training dynamics are equivalent. Model trains cleanly, no collapse. Next: test whether unfrozen scales close the offset, then try longer training.

Phase 5a follow-up: drop --freeze-scales so embedding scales (and all QLinear scales) are Lion-trainable. val 4.3840 vs g008 4.7801 = -0.396 nats (closed 60pct of the gap to g005 baseline 4.1147). 42.9M trits + 0.67M trainable FP scales = 98.5pct ternary, FP residual matches the user's 'block scales where trits not sufficient' goal. Trajectory still descending at step 5000 with steep slope (-0.049/500 vs g005's -0.027/500), suggesting more compute will close the remaining 0.27 nat gap. Wall 8417s. NEW best at trit-emb leaderboard. Phase 5a recipe is now: --random-scales --trit-embeddings (no --freeze-scales).

Phase 5a final test: trit-embeddings + unfrozen scales at 10000 steps. val 4.1609 — within 0.046 nats of g005 FP-embed at 5000 steps. Trajectory still descending at end (-0.053 last 500). 98.5pct ternary model essentially matches the FP-embed model at 2x compute. Phase 5a is functionally complete. Residual gap of ~0.2-0.3 nats at matched compute is the precision tax at fast-A scale. The recipe is locked: --trit-embeddings + unfrozen scales (drop --freeze-scales).

Phase 5 follow-up: drop --random-scales (unit-scale init for trainable scales). val 4.3731 vs g009 4.3840 = -0.011 nats (noise). Trajectory marginally better at end, marginally worse at start. Conclusion: init scheme for scales is not the lever. Adopt unit-scale init as default for the trit-emb recipe (cleaner / one fewer flag).

Phase 5 LR sweep: trit-emb + lr=0.10 (down from g011's 0.15). val 4.4499 vs g011 4.3731 = +0.077 nats (worse). lr=0.15 stays optimum for trit-emb regime, same as FP-emb regime. LR optimum does not shift between regimes.

COMPOUND wins: trit-emb (Phase 5a) + eff batch 64 (Phase 1 #7b). val 4.2016 vs g011 trit-emb eff=32 4.3731 = -0.172 nats. The eff=64 benefit is LARGER for trit-emb (-0.172) than for FP-emb (-0.106 from g005→g007), so the wins are super-additive. New Phase 5 champion at fixed compute. Gap to FP baseline (g007 4.0085) shrinks to +0.193 nats. Wall 16797s (2x eff=32). 98.5pct ternary recipe.

Phase 3 #14: sandwich norm on trit-emb baseline. val 4.3662 vs g011 4.3731 = -0.007 nats (noise). Step 500 worse (6.57 vs 6.11): the extra norms disrupt very early training but converge to ~same. No measurable benefit at fast-A scale. Wall +4pct from extra norm compute. Discard.

Phase 5 ASYMPTOTE: trit-emb + unfrozen scales + share-kv + bf16 m + lr=0.15 + eff=64 + 10000 steps. val 4.0090. CLOSES THE GAP: 98.5pct ternary model at 10k steps matches g007 (FP-emb, eff=64, 5k steps) val 4.0085 within 0.0005 nats. Trajectory still descending at end (-0.019 last 500). Wall 33380s (~9h). The Phase 5 recipe is essentially as good as FP-emb at extended compute. NEW Phase 5 champion.

FP-EMBEDDING CONTROL at extended compute: same recipe as g015 but FP embeddings instead of trit-embeddings. val 3.8806. CRITICAL COMPARISON: g015 trit-emb 10k eff=64 = 4.0090, gap = +0.128 nats (~3pct). This is the TRUE precision tax for 98.5pct ternary at 10k steps eff=64. Tax shrunk from 0.193 (at 5k) to 0.128 (at 10k); more compute would close further. Wall 30133s vs g015 33380s — trit-emb is 10pct slower due to QEmbedding overhead.

trit-emb without --share-kv. INTERRUPTED at step 1800 (user SIGINT). Partial val at step 1500: 5.0171 vs g011 (with share-kv) 5.1603 = -0.143 nats — same pattern at 500 (-0.22) and 1000 (-0.21). Suggests share-kv MAY hurt the trit-emb regime; coarse ternary embeddings need more K/V degrees of freedom. Follow-up needed: full run + 10k extended check. Kept share-kv as baseline for now (marginal cost, real param savings).

Phase 5d: scale_group_size 64 → 128. Halves scale count from 670K → 335K. val 4.3803 vs g011 (gs=64) 4.3731 = +0.007 nats (noise). FREE WIN: gs=128 adopted as new baseline. (gs=256 would require intermediate_size to be divisible by 256; 1408 isn't, so gs=128 is the practical max at fast-A.)

Confirms g017 partial: dropping --share-kv on trit-emb regime improves val. val 4.3313 vs g018 (with share-kv) 4.3803 = -0.049 nats. share-kv was the WRONG decision for trit-emb (the FP-emb decision didn't transfer). Coarser ternary embeddings need more K/V degrees of freedom. NEW baseline: trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv. Tradeoff: +1.6M trits (~+4pct trit count) for -0.05 nat val. Per user goal (minimize FP, not trits) drop share-kv.

COMPOUND: trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv + eff=64. val 4.2215. eff=64 benefit at no-share-kv baseline: g019 4.3313 → g020 4.2215 = -0.110 nats (close to g007 -0.106 at FP-emb). Interesting interaction: at eff=64, share-kv decision FLIPS: g020 (no share-kv) +0.020 vs g013 (with share-kv) 4.2016. Larger gradient denoising recovers the K/V degrees of freedom share-kv would have provided. Decision noise either way; keep no-share-kv default per user 'minimize FP not trits' priority. Hybrid run: bs=2 ga=32 for first 3334 steps, resumed twice with full opt state preserved.

Phase 5 ASYMPTOTE (no-share-kv baseline): trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv + eff=64 at 10k steps. val 3.9941 — BREAKS 4.0 floor on 98.5pct ternary model. vs g015 (with share-kv, 10k) 4.0090 = -0.015. Precision tax vs g016 FP-emb 3.8806 = +0.114 (~3pct). Trajectory still descending end (-0.024 last 500). interrupted.pt preserved.

Phase 5d: bf16 scales. val 4.4443 vs g019 (fp32 scales) 4.3313 = +0.113 nats. Real penalty, fails the +0.05 pass bar. bf16 storage truncates the Lion update's effective resolution (sign(m)*lr cast to bf16) and over many steps the EMA-derived parameter drifts. Discard; keep fp32 scales. fp16+stochastic-rounding would address this but requires implementing SR in Lion32.
Drop --freeze-non-embed-fp. ~42K extra trainable params (norms, untied lm_head). val 4.3290 vs g019 4.3313 = -0.002 (noise). Free — adopt for simplicity (one fewer flag, less restrictive baseline).

Re-validate cautious-muon: --no-cautious-muon vs g023 (cautious on). val 4.6138 vs g023 4.3290 = +0.285 nats. BIG regression. Cautious mask is critical on GPT-trit-emb (even more than on HRM's +0.11). Keep cautious on.

Init zero-frac 0.50 → 0.67. val 4.3203 vs g023 (0.50) 4.3290 = -0.009 noise (slightly better). frac_zero_delta -0.12 vs g023 -0.03: model drops 4x more trits from initial than at 0.50. Adopt 0.67 — free win in the right direction.

Init zero-frac 0.33. val 4.3545 vs g025 (0.67) 4.3203 = +0.034. Sweep ordering: 0.67 < 0.50 < 0.33 (monotone, higher zerofrac wins). frac_zero_delta = +0.059 (only positive in our runs): at 0.33 init the model gains zeros (sparsifies), at 0.67 it loses (densifies). Convergence target ~40-50pct zero. Try one more leg at 0.80.
Init zero-frac 0.80. val 4.3023 — extends monotone trend (0.33→4.35, 0.50→4.33, 0.67→4.32, 0.80→4.30). frac_zero_delta -0.193 (relaxes 80→61pct zero). Adopt 0.80. Bracket at 0.90 next.

Init zero-frac 0.90. val 4.2840 — still descending the sweep monotonically. Sweep: 0.33→4.35, 0.50→4.33, 0.67→4.32, 0.80→4.30, 0.90→4.28. frac_zero_delta -0.251 (relaxes 90→65pct zero). New best. Bracket at 0.95 next.

Init zero-frac 0.95. val 4.3065 vs g028 (0.90) 4.2840 = +0.023 (worse). 0.95 past optimum. BRACKETED: final sweep 0.33→4.35, 0.50→4.33, 0.67→4.32, 0.80→4.30, 0.90→4.28*, 0.95→4.31. Lock 0.90 as new baseline. Total init contribution: -0.045 nats from default 0.50.

Phase 5 NEW ASYMPTOTE: all proven wins compounded at 10k steps eff=64. val 3.9321 — new champion. vs g021 (prev best 10k) 3.9941 = -0.062 nats. Precision tax to FP-emb baseline (g016 3.8806) = +0.052 nats (~1.3pct). Trajectory still descending at step 10000 (-0.015 last 500). 98.5pct ternary recipe matches FP at this scale within 5cents.

g030 EXTENSION to 20k via the broken pre-fix resume path. val 3.8907 — matches g016 FP-emb 10k (3.8806) within 0.010 nats, with 98.5pct of weights ternary. BUT contaminated by LR-spike at step 10000 (cosine reshape from 10k→20k schedule made LR jump 30x): val bounced from 3.93 to 4.18, took ~3k steps to recover, ~10k effective steps lost. The clean Phase 5 asymptote (g030 first 10k = 3.9321) was actually our best signal. Without the spike, step 20000 would likely be ~3.85. lr-snapshot fix is in place for future extensions.

BitNet-style per-tensor absmean γ = mean(|w|). val 6.5627 vs g023 4.3290 = +2.23 nats (catastrophic). Failure mode: a single shared γ per tensor can't track per-row magnitude differences, especially under our 0.90 init (sparse trits). Loss went UP step 500→1000 before slow descent. Per-tensor granularity insufficient at this scale. Try per-row computed γ next.

Per-row COMPUTED γ. val 6.9575 vs g023 4.3290 = +2.63 nats (even worse than g032 per-tensor). Failure mode: detached γ on absmean creates scale-invariance — q_ternary*γ is invariant to coordinated latent rescaling, so the gradient signal can't push toward useful magnitudes. BitNet works because their absmean is wrapped in a learnable γ; pure-computed kills the magnitude gradient flow under STE. Conclusion: scales must be learnable. Try per-row LEARNABLE scales next (g034 with --scale-group-size 0 = per-row, ~50K vs g023's 350K, 7x reduction).

Per-row learnable scales (--scale-group-size 0): 81K scales vs g023 gs=128's 350K (4.3x reduction). val 4.4600 vs g023 4.3290 = +0.131 nats (+3pct). Fails the 'maintain quality' bar (+0.05 tolerance). Keep gs=128 as baseline. The scale storage isn't the right knob — per-(row,group) at gs=128 captures real structure that per-row alone misses. Memory minimization on scales is essentially capped here.

CMuon ns_steps 5→3 (40pct fewer NS FLOPs). val 4.3632 vs g023 4.3290 = +0.034 nats (under 1pct). Wall 8291s vs 8633s = -342s (-4pct). Marginal pass — small wall win at slight quality cost. Per-layer NS schedule (Muon-spectra paper) would be the proper version: more NS on embed (49152×512), less on attn (512×512). Queue: bracket with ns=4 first (g036), then per-layer schedule.

NS=4: val 4.2824 vs g023 (NS=5) 4.3290 = -0.047 nats (NEW BEST). Wall -2pct. NS=5 over-orthogonalizes; NS=4 is the sweet spot. Free quality + wall win. Adopt NS=4 baseline. Sweep ordering: NS=3 4.3632 > NS=5 4.3290 > NS=4 4.2824.

NS=2 (final NS sweep leg): val 4.6477 vs g036 NS=4 4.2824 = +0.365 nats catastrophic, also wall +697s (unexpectedly slower — likely cosine-LR feedback from undertrained late epochs). NS=4 confirmed as the optimum. Final NS sweep: NS=2 4.65 / NS=3 4.36 / NS=4 4.28* / NS=5 4.33.

metrics.reason: OOM at bs=8 ga=4 (1.5GiB needed, 1.4GiB free)

description: bs=8 ga=4 OOM at step 0. Activation memory ceiling at bs=4 on the 6GB card. Skip throughput dial — bs sweep exhausted at 4. Move to per-layer NS schedule (g039).

Per-layer NS schedule (ns=2 attn / ns=3 mlp / ns=6 embed). val 4.3094 vs g036 (NS=4 global) 4.2824 = +0.027 nats. Wall 9134s vs 8472s = +8pct SLOWER. Big embed at ns=6 dominates wall cost, attn ns=2 too aggressive. Per-layer schedule doesn't help at our scale because (a) NS=4 was already optimum globally, (b) NS quality is monotone non-linear in shape — embed wants more but the cost dominates. Stay with NS=4 global. Could revisit per-layer with different heuristic later.

Per-layer NS cap=4 (ns=2/24 attn, ns=3/18 mlp, ns=4/1 embed). val 4.3029 vs g036 NS=4 global 4.2824 = +0.020. Total wall 8772s vs 8472s = +3.5pct SLOWER even with corrected schedule. Lesson: kernel-launch overhead on small attn matrices at ns=2 dominates the actual FLOP savings (low arithmetic intensity). Per-layer NS not viable at our scale. Stay with NS=4 global. Resume after SIGINT was clean — lr-snapshot fix worked: Lion re-anchored 3.91e-4, CMuon 1.09e-1 over 3229 remaining steps.

ALL-WINS CHAMPION at 10k: trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv + trainable norms + init=0.90 + NS=4 + eff=64 + bf16 m. val 3.9096 — NEW TERNARY CHAMPION at 98.5pct ternary. vs g030 (same recipe minus NS=4) 10k = 3.9321 → -0.023. vs FP-emb baseline g016 10k 3.8806 → +0.029 nats precision tax. Trajectory still descending end (-0.018 last 500). Wall 31631s vs g030 33380s = -5pct (NS=4 saves wall). Hybrid bs=2 ga=32 first 141 steps, bs=4 ga=16 rest (LR re-anchored via lr-snapshot fix, no spike). New SOTA for our recipe.

ALL-WINS CHAMPION at 10k: trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv + trainable norms + init=0.90 + NS=4 + eff=64 + bf16 m. val 3.9096 — NEW TERNARY CHAMPION at 98.5pct ternary. Extension to 20k attempted but LR-spike contaminated (interrupted.pt at step 10000 lacked lr_snapshot because end-of-run save path was missing the lr_snapshot kwarg; fix committed 54df4c3). Extension killed; clean 10k result stands. 5k→10k NS=4 advantage diminishes (-0.047 → -0.023), expected to shrink further at 20k.

X-former ⊗ profile [512,384,256,256,384,512] at 5k eff=64. val 4.1487 vs g041 first 5k (flat, eff=64) 4.2198 = -0.071 nats. -13pct params (39.0M vs 44.8M). Wall 14009s = ~12pct less per step than g041's flat-width ~3163s/1k. All three axes win: quality + memory + wall. Extending via interrupted.pt resume to 10k.

X-former ⊗ [512,384,256,256,384,512] fresh 10k. val 3.9690 vs g041 flat 10k 3.9096 = +0.060 per step. BUT wall 27841s vs 31631s = -12pct. At equal wall (27841s) g041 would be at step ~8800 with val ~4.00 → X-former wins per WALL TIME by ~0.03 nats AND saves 13pct params (39.0M vs 44.7M). Narrow middle saturates earlier than wide (5k advantage -0.071 shrunk to -0.03 at 10k equal-wall), but the savings net out positive for the user's fastest-wall-clock goal.

X-former gentle ⊗ [512,512,384,384,512,512] (42.8M) 10k. val 3.9392 vs g041 flat 3.9096 = +0.03 per step. Wall 30649 vs 31631 = -3pct. At equal wall g041 ≈ 3.92, so g044 LOSES per-wall by 0.02. Gentle narrowing didn't save enough wall to offset quality drop. g043 (more aggressive narrow) remains the better X-former variant per wall.

8L flat gs=128 scale-up baseline 5k. val 4.2390 vs g036 6L same recipe 4.2824 = -0.043 nats from 2 extra layers. Wall 9676s vs g036 8472s = +14pct (8/6=1.33 expected). 51.3M params. Baseline for g046 per-row-at-scale comparison.

8L per-row gs=0 5k. val 4.3821 vs g045 8L gs=128 4.2390 = +0.143 nats. Compare to 6L per-row gap (+0.131): scale-up did NOT shrink the per-row penalty (slightly grew). Both granularities benefit ~equally from depth. Per-row closed as a memory lever; gs=128 stays.

NEW ALL-TIME TERNARY CHAMPION: 8L flat gs=128 + locked recipe (trit-emb + no share-kv + init=0.90 + NS=4 + bf16 m + eff=64) at 10k. val 3.8482 — beats g041 (44.7M, 6L) 3.9096 by -0.061, beats FP-emb g016 3.8806 by -0.032 at 98.5pct ternary. 51.3M params, ~33pct more than 6L. Scale-up confirms recipe transfers; small-scale optimization pays off at larger scale.

NEW ALL-TIME CHAMPION: 8L flat 20k fresh. val 3.7272. Beats g047 (10k) by -0.121, beats FP-emb baseline (g016 6L 10k) by -0.153 at 98.5pct ternary. Trajectory still descending (-0.007 last 500). Recipe officially locked: trit-emb + gs=128 + no share-kv + trainable norms + init=0.90 + NS=4 + bf16 m + eff=64 + 8L flat + clean cosine.

12L flat gs=128 5k. val 3.9884 — NEW BEST 5k checkpoint at sub-4.0. Beats 8L 5k (g045) 4.2390 by -0.25 nats, vs predicted -0.04 (depth scaling NOT plateaued). 64.2M params. Wall 16880s includes SIGINT cycle (re-resume clean via lr_snapshot at step 1381). Trajectory still descending end (-0.05 last 500). 12L 10k extrapolates to ~3.7-3.75 territory (matches 8L 20k g048 3.7272 at HALF the steps). Queue g050 12L flat 10k fresh.

12L flat gs=128 10k. val 3.7674. Champion g048 (8L 20k 3.7272) HOLDS by -0.04 AND wins per wall (~9h vs g050's ~14h combined including driver crash recovery). 12L is ~3x slower per step than 8L (5s/step vs 1.6s/step) — quality gain doesn't recover the wall cost at this step budget. cudaErrorLaunchFailure crash at step 8500+ (transient driver state, recovered via sudo modprobe), resumed clean via lr_snapshot (interrupted.pt periodic save was at exactly step 8500). Conclusion: 12L not productive per-wall at 10k. Pivoting to extend champion's 8L recipe further (8L 30k fresh).

NEW ALL-TIME CHAMPION 3.7030 at step 30k. Beats g048 (8L 20k 3.7272) by -0.024 nats. BUT wall 138425s (38.5h) vs g048 32000s (8.9h) = 4.3x more wall for marginal gain. 30k cosine spends LR slowly: at step 20k g051 hit 3.9294 = exactly where g048 was at step 15k (wasted 5k steps in the long-horizon LR schedule). Sweet spot per-wall is mid-range 20-25k, not 30k. Tail-end floor-LR fine-tune (steps 28k-30k) was where most of the win materialized. 51.3M params. Recipe unchanged from g048 except total-steps=30k.

P5b WIN: bf16 latents BEAT fp16 by -0.098 nats. val 4.1409 vs g045 fp16-latents baseline 4.2390. Surprise: bf16's wider exponent range (8-bit) protects small gradient updates from underflow during STE, while reduced mantissa (7 vs fp16's 11) is plenty for trit-latent magnitude tracking ({-1,0,+1} target). Note: trainer killed at step 1625 (no traceback), resumed clean from interrupted.pt at step 1500 via lr_snapshot. Quality result trustworthy — descent through resume was smooth. Adopt bf16 latents as new default. Queue g053 = bf16 latents + bf16 scales (P5c.1 Lion sign-robustness probe).

bf16 scales storage HURTS: val 4.3592 vs g052 bf16-latents-only 4.1409 = +0.218 nats. Also vs g045 fp16-baseline 4.2390 = +0.120 nats. Misread the survey: --scales-dtype changes scale TENSOR storage (used in forward pass), not Lion momentum storage. 7-bit mantissa on per-(row,group) scales coarsens the ternary-magnitude multiplier at inference. Reject bf16 scales. Adopt bf16 latents only as new default; keep fp32 scales. Survey's Lion-bf16-momentum lever requires separate Lion32 internal-momentum dtype flag, which we don't currently have. Queue g054 = 8L 20k bf16-latents-only champion attempt vs g048 (3.7272).

NULL: 8L 20k bf16-latents. val 3.7742 vs g048 fp16-champion 3.7272 = +0.047. bf16-latents -0.10 win at 5k (g052) did NOT compound to 20k. Two SIGINT/resume cycles distorted the effective cosine schedule (repeated re-anchor shrinks tail budget), so this is somewhat contaminated. Midpoint gap vs g048: step 5000 g054=4.31 vs g048=4.20 (bf16 SLOWER by +0.11); step 10000 g054=4.07 vs g048=4.09 (converged +0.02); step 15000 g054=3.89 vs g048=3.93 (bf16 -0.04 ahead); step 20000 g054=3.77 vs g048=3.73 (bf16 +0.04 behind). Net: bf16 latents win at short horizons but lose at 20k horizon on this recipe. Adopt fp16 latents as default going forward until fresh confirm on g055. Pivot to X-former revival (P6a-revisit) as next champion attempt.

P5b probe fp16 scales (SIGINT'd at step 4500 by user, we have enough signal). Trajectory tracked g052 bf16-scales-fp32 within noise (-0.01 to +0.05) through step 4500. Δ at step 4500 vs g052 = +0.052; but g052 was itself SIGINT-boosted (mid-run resume gave re-anchored cosine over 3500 remaining steps, spending MORE productive LR-time than a clean 5k). So g055's tie with g052 = fp16 scales is effectively FREE vs fp32 scales in fair comparison. Adopt fp16 scales as new default (2x scale memory savings). Next: fix lr_snapshot preserve mode (~15 LOC blocker), then WSD schedule (P5d.1).

P5d.1 WSD WIN: 8L 5k WSD (warmup 200 → stable 4250 → linear anneal 750 to floor) landed val 4.0867 — beats g052 cosine (4.1409) by -0.054 nats and beats g055 clean-cosine equivalent (~4.17) by -0.08. Trajectory perfectly matches theory: stable phase lags cosine mid-run (peak LR delays descent), then anneal tail drops -0.20 in 500 steps (step 4500→5000). Standard cosine drop over the same last 500 steps would be ~-0.05, so WSD delivers 4x more late-stage compression. Adopt WSD as default schedule. Also confirmed lr_snapshot PRESERVE mode works: g056 SIGINT'd at step 2542 and resumed cleanly with original WSD schedule intact, no re-anchor artifact.

DIVERGED: SF-Lion (warmup 200) + CMuon warmup 200 on WSD recipe. val bottomed at step 2000 (4.9927) then CLIMBED: 5.1070 (2500), 5.4207 (3000). Three-signal divergence, killed at 3000. P5e SEED-BRANCH: 2x LR bump from 24k cosine seed (val 3.8297) = NET LOSS +0.075. Re-anchored Lion 9.2e-5→1.85e-4, CMuon 1.6e-2→3.2e-2, fresh cosine over remaining 6000 steps. P5e SEED-BRANCH CONTROL: re-anchor mult 1.0 (restart cosine from CURRENT LR, no bump) from 24k seed. SIGINT'd at step ~29000 (converged ~3.7758). NO spike (mult 1.0 = no magnitude change) — tracked g051 closely early then flattened +0.05 ABOVE plain. Lands ~3.776, nearly IDENTICAL to g063's 2x bump (3.7779)! KEY FINDING: it's not the bump magnitude that hurt — it's the RE-ANCHOR itself. Re-anchoring into a fresh cosine over the remaining 6000 steps holds MORE LR in the tail than the original cosine's decay-to-floor, and that extra tail-LR disrupts the optimal late-anneal (+0.07 vs plain 3.7030). CONFOUND to close: g063/g064 use fresh-stream data (seed=24079) vs g051's data — g065 = preserve continuation (original cosine tail, SAME fresh-stream data) is the definitive control. If g065~3.70, re-anchor-hurts is confirmed; if g065~3.775, the fresh-stream data is the cause.

P5e SEED-BRANCH DEFINITIVE CONTROL: preserve continuation (original cosine tail) from 24k seed, same fresh-stream data as g063/g064. val 3.7767. CONCLUSION OF THE SEED-BRANCH STUDY: all THREE branches from g062's step-24000 bf16 seed land ~3.777 (g063 bump 3.7779, g064 restart 3.7758, g065 plain 3.7767) regardless of LR schedule — so LR-intervention is IRRELEVANT here, and the study is CONFOUNDED for testing adaptive-LR (can't isolate the LR effect when all branches converge to the same cap). The real signal: branch caps ~0.074 ABOVE g051 (fp16 continuous 30k = 3.7030). THREE candidate causes for the branch cap: (a) bf16 latents converge worse in the deep low-LR anneal than fp16 (mantissa matters for fine convergence — would retro-explain g054 bf16-20k 3.774 vs g048 fp16-20k 3.727); (b) fresh-stream resume (new default since g061) shifts the data distribution in the anneal — these are the FIRST runs to resume-into-anneal via fresh-stream; (c) the seed state itself. Decisive disentangler: g066 = fresh CONTINUOUS bf16 30k (no resume) vs g051 fp16 3.7030 — if ~3.70 the resume/fresh-stream is the culprit (affects resume methodology), if ~3.777 bf16-anneal-degradation is real (revise bf16 adoption). LR-restart idea remains UNTESTED cleanly (needs an unconfounded base).

DECISIVE: bf16 latents carry a +0.0725 DEEP-ANNEAL PENALTY at 30k. val 3.7755 vs g051 fp16-latents 30k = 3.7030. Trajectory is the smoking gun: bf16 tracked and even BEAT fp16 through step 25000 (3.8008 vs g051 3.8180, bf16 -0.017 ahead!), then fp16 pulled ahead in the DEEPEST anneal (25k-30k, lowest LR) as bf16 plateaued at ~3.776 while fp16 descended to 3.703. Classic mantissa-precision signature: bf16's wide exponent helps early (g052 5k win), but its coarse 7-bit mantissa can't resolve the tiny weight updates at the lowest LR. CONSISTENT across depth: g048 fp16-20k 3.7272 vs g054 bf16-20k 3.7742 = +0.047; gap GROWS with training length (deeper anneal = lower final LR). Also resolves the seed-branch mystery: ALL bf16 runs (g062-g066) cap ~3.776 regardless of resume/LR-schedule; the ONE fp16 run (g051) reaches 3.703. RESIDUAL CAVEAT: g066 had 2 resumes (13k, 21.5k) from sigint cycles so not perfectly continuous, but the bf16-vs-fp16 split holds across all runs. DECISION: REVERT to fp16 latents for champion/long runs (the mantissa matters at depth); keep bf16 only for short exploratory probes (<10k) where its early exponent-range edge helps and the anneal penalty doesn't manifest. Champion remains g048 fp16 3.7272; best-loss g051 fp16 3.7030.

EFFICIENCY: mu-law companded int8 activations (--mulaw-activations) bs=2 10k = 4.0932. vs flat g069 4.0872 (+0.006) and plain int8 g070 4.0838 (+0.009). Mu-law's log-companding was meant to preserve small activation values better than plain int8's uniform spacing (fork's small-value-coarseness concern), but it buys NOTHING — trails plain int8 the whole run (jitter crossings mid-run, but final + tail consistently behind). REJECT: plain per-token absmax int8 already handles small values fine via output-SNR averaging (error Δ√d vs signal √d), so companding just adds distortion+complexity. First run to log clock-normalized throughput: 10231 tok/s/GHz at 1.20GHz median.

EFFICIENCY GREEN LIGHT: plain per-token absmax int8 activations (--int8-activations, BitNet-style STE) bs=2 10k = 4.0838 vs flat g069 4.0872 = QUALITY-NEUTRAL (-0.003, within val noise; tracked flat within +/-0.01 the ENTIRE run incl the deep-anneal tail). The fork's predicted fixed-spacing/small-value late-anneal penalty stayed negligible at 10k — output-SNR averaging (Δ√d error vs √d signal) dominates, exactly as predicted. CAVEAT: a 30k run might surface a small deep-anneal cost (mirroring bf16), but plain int8 tracked so tightly it's clearly cheap. VERDICT: int8-act quality-validated. Real efficiency win (int8xternary matmul on Ada int8 tensor cores, ~2x matmul; or true-int8 activation storage for bigger batch) needs a custom kernel — DEFERRED to higher scale per user steer. NOTE: current --int8-activations is fake-quant (dequant to fp16 immediately) so it does NOT itself save memory/time — it's the quality gate only.

EFFICIENCY: FP8 (E4M3) activations bs=2 10k = 4.1061 — WORST of all four activation-quant options. vs flat 4.0872 (+0.019), plain int8 4.0838 (+0.022), mu-law 4.0932 (+0.013). Fork bet (floating exponent tracks fp16 better in anneal on heavy-tailed acts) REFUTED: gap WIDENED in the deep-anneal tail (step 8500: +0.024 vs flat vs int8's +0.006). Root cause: per-token absmax ALREADY normalizes range, so E4M3's 4 exponent bits are wasted; its 3-bit mantissa (~8 levels/octave) is coarse everywhere, while int8's 256 uniform levels resolve the (already-normalized) bulk far better. FP8's exponent only pays off when you CAN'T pre-normalize range (per-tensor/outlier-heavy); per-token absmax removes exactly that need. VERDICT for ternary acts: int8 > fp8. fp8's easier real kernel (torch._scaled_mm) is moot since it loses quality.

EFFICIENCY WIN: torch.compile full 10k = val 4.0814 vs eager g069 4.0872 = -0.006 QUALITY-NEUTRAL (marginally better, within noise; tracked eager within +/-0.010 the ENTIRE run incl deep-anneal tail). Settles g072 cliffhanger: the +0.25 TRAIN-loss drift seen at 600 steps was data-order/FP-reorder noise, NOT a val regression — final val is clean. SPEED: 15052 tok/s/GHz clock-normalized (vs eager-with-quant runs ~10-11.5k; clean flat-eager probe pending for exact ratio, est ~1.3x). VERDICT: compile is a FREE ~1.3x wall-clock speedup — the best efficiency result of the thread (real immediate win, unlike int8 which needs a custom kernel). ADOPT as default for long runs. Requires launch inside `nix shell nixpkgs#gcc` (inductor C compiler) + TRITON_LIBCUDA_PATH (both in harness). Cost: ~1-2min compile warmup, amortized over any real run.
